title: The Rats and the Iron
logline: A merchant whose friend claims that rats ate his iron answers with an equally absurd tale, that a hawk carried off the friend's son, and so wins back the truth, his iron and the friendship.
moral: A lie is best exposed by holding up its own mirror; an absurd excuse invites an absurd answer, and honesty restores what trickery took.
tone: Dry comedy of manners: a deadpan merchant, a sweating liar, two ridiculous picture clouds that match each other, and a warm, forgiving ending.

beats.summary: A merchant in a busy city owns a great stack of iron.
His old friend promises to keep it safe (the promise pose).
Short of money, the friend sells the iron and pockets the price.
The lie: rats came in and ate all the iron.
The merchant swallows the accusation in front of people and starts to plan.
He takes the friend's son somewhere safe and feeds him.
His answer to the worried father: a big hawk carried the boy away.
In a city where rats eat iron, a hawk can carry a child.
Silence: the friend sees that the merchant knows the truth.
He confesses the sale and promises to repay.
The boy is home safe; father and son embrace; the debt is paid.
Neither speaks again of iron-eating rats or child-carrying hawks.

sets.description: The planned city street (AN-095): skyline, house fronts, clear palette. This story needs the friend's house front: facade x 380..1000 with a storeroom double door (x 420..610, y 640..900, bar and padlock, can open to show the interior), the house door (x 720..820) and a window (x 860..940, y 620..700); to the left an open street with a road running to a far city gate (about x 120, y 820). A second framing without the storeroom door (wall and palm) serves S8, and the merchant's own door S9/S10. Dusk palette for S18. Coordinates are targets for the new drawing; measure on the set once built.

Cutaway interior of the storeroom: plank floor at y 900, stone back wall, one small barred window high on the left with a light shaft, a shelf with two jars, the open doorway on the right (x 600..900). States: full (iron stack at x 180..420) and empty (dust outlines of the stack, a cobweb in the corner). Also drawn small inside the clouds.
The planned merchantHouse variant of palaceHall (AN-095): arched interior, window light from the left, tiled floor at y 900, a cushion at x 620 and a low table at x 520. No treasure curtain needed.

props.description: A stack of dark blue-grey iron bars with white glints: each bar 120 x 18 units, stacked 5 wide and up to 6 rows on the cart; fields n (bars left), glint (index), bites (notches eaten out of the top row).
Two-wheeled wooden handcart, bed 200 x 30 units, wheels radius 42 turning from distance travelled, two handles.
The planned purse and coinPile (AN-095): drawstring purse with a fill field (0 empty and flat, 1 fat), gold coins.
The planned ball (KD-008): red and white, radius 16.
Round brass tray (radius 60) with a flat bread, a small pile of dates and a cup.

ending.description: After the last word (157.24) the real rat tries the iron nail and hurts its tooth (TINK! OW!), which answers the lie one last time without a word. THE END appears at 158.6 in the evening sky above the three figures on the doorstep and holds to 161.0; they keep breathing and blinking and the boy waves once.

subtitles.ar: كان تاجر يعيش في مدينة مزدحمة، ولديه كمية كبيرة من الحديد.|أراد أن يسافر للعمل، فطلب من صديق قديم|أن يحفظ الحديد في بيته حتى يعود.|وافق الصديق ووعده بذلك.
subtitles.en: A merchant lived in a busy city and owned a large amount of iron.|He needed to travel for work, so he asked an old friend|to keep the iron in his house until he returned.|The friend agreed and promised to do so.

subtitles.ar: غاب التاجر أشهرًا، وخلال غيابه احتاج الصديق إلى المال.|باع الحديد وأخذ ثمنه لنفسه.|وعندما عاد التاجر وسأله عن أمانته،|قال الصديق: «حدث شيء غريب جدًا!»
subtitles.en: The merchant was away for months. During that time, his friend needed money,|so he sold the iron and kept the payment.|When the merchant returned and asked for his property,|the friend said, “Something very strange happened!”

subtitles.ar: سأله التاجر: «ماذا حدث؟»|قال الصديق: «وضعت الحديد في المخزن،|لكن الفئران دخلت وأكلته كله!»|تعجب التاجر كثيرًا، لكنه لم يتهم صديقه بالكذب أمام الناس.
subtitles.en: “What happened?” the merchant asked.|“I put the iron in the storeroom,” said the friend,|“but rats came inside and ate all of it!”|The merchant was astonished, but he did not call his friend a liar in front of everyone.

subtitles.ar: بعد أيام، التقى التاجر بابن صديقه في الطريق.|أخذه إلى مكان آمن، وأعطاه طعامًا،|وطلب منه أن ينتظر هناك قليلًا.|ثم عاد وحده إلى بيت صديقه.
subtitles.en: A few days later, the merchant met his friend’s son on the road.|He took the boy to a safe place, gave him food,|and asked him to wait there for a while.|Then he returned alone to his friend’s house.

subtitles.ar: سأله الرجل بقلق: «هل رأيت ابني؟|إنه لم يعد إلى البيت!»|قال التاجر: «رأيته في الطريق،|لكن صقرًا كبيرًا نزل من السماء وحمله بعيدًا.»
subtitles.en: The man asked anxiously, “Have you seen my son?|He has not come home!”|The merchant answered, “I saw him on the road,|but a large hawk flew down from the sky and carried him away.”

subtitles.ar: صاح الرجل: «هذا مستحيل!|كيف يستطيع صقر أن يحمل طفلًا؟»|أجابه التاجر بهدوء: «في مدينة تأكل فيها الفئران الحديد،|لا أستغرب أن يحمل صقر طفلًا!»
subtitles.en: “That is impossible!” the man cried.|“How could a hawk carry a child?”|The merchant answered calmly, “In a city where rats can eat iron,|I would not be surprised if a hawk could carry a child!”

subtitles.ar: سكت الصديق، وفهم أن التاجر عرف الحقيقة.|قال أخيرًا: «الفئران لم تأكل الحديد.|لقد بعته عندما احتجت إلى المال.|سأعيد إليك الحديد أو ثمنه كاملًا.»
subtitles.en: The friend fell silent and realized that the merchant knew the truth.|Finally he said, “The rats did not eat the iron.|I sold it when I needed money.|I will return your iron or pay its full value.”

subtitles.ar: عاد التاجر بالولد سالمًا، وفرح أبوه عندما رآه.|دفع الرجل ثمن الحديد إلى التاجر كما وعد.|وبعد ذلك، لم يتحدث أحد منهما|عن فئران تأكل الحديد أو صقر يحمل الأطفال.
subtitles.en: The merchant brought the boy back safely, and his father was delighted to see him.|The man paid the merchant for the iron as promised.|After that, neither of them spoke again|of rats that ate iron or hawks that carried children.

new_assets.name: rat
new_assets.description: Small comic rat for this and any later fable with mice or rats. Pose fields: ph and amp (scurry), sit, sniff (nose up, whiskers twitch), chew, bite, fat (0..1 belly), roll (on its back), bib, tailCurl, plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: One function rat(ctx, P): ellipse body, circle head with a pointed snout, two round pink ears, a tapered Bezier tail, four short legs driven by walk(); eye through eye2 so gaze and lid work; wrap with acting(). Registry entry and catalogue poses.

new_assets.name: hawk (bird kind)
new_assets.description: A bird of prey as a new kind on the Library bird: palette, hooked beak, heavy brow, talons that can grip.
new_assets.implementation: Add BIRD.hawk palette and optional fields hook (beak shape) and talons (0..1 open) to bird(); defaults unchanged so the regression test stays identical. Flight on a Bezier path as in the Lark flyBz, flap from climb rate.

new_assets.name: storeroom
new_assets.description: Cutaway storeroom interior with full and empty states (see sets).
new_assets.implementation: bake() the wall, floor, window and shelf once; draw the stack, dust outlines and cobweb as state layers; draw the same function scaled inside thoughtCloud.

new_assets.name: marketStreet
new_assets.description: The planned AN-095 street, with a house-front module that has an opening storeroom door.
new_assets.implementation: Reuse the planned set; add a houseFront(ctx, {doorOpen, storeOpen, padlock}) module of flat rects and a damped swing() on the door leaves. Skyline from nightCity shapes in a day palette.

new_assets.name: ironBars, handcart
new_assets.description: The iron stack and the cart that carries it (see props).
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rects with a highlight stroke, drawn in rows; bites are circles cut with destination-out on a baked layer keyed by time; cart from rects and two spoked circles.

new_assets.name: person child option
new_assets.description: A child built on the person figure: s 0.62 with head 1.25x, no facial hair, chew field (alternating cheek puffs).
new_assets.implementation: Optional P.child and P.chew fields on person(); defaults off.

new_assets.name: foodTray
new_assets.description: Brass tray with bread, dates and a cup.
new_assets.implementation: Ellipse tray, half-disc bread, six small ovals, a cup from a trapezoid.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: The planned generic picture cloud, used here as a telling cloud with a tail toward the speaker; two sizes (520 x 370 and about 410 x 300).
new_assets.implementation: Scalloped outline from circles on a rounded rect, white fill, clip, then drawInside(ctx, t) in the cloud's own coordinates; scale key for pop in and out.

new_assets.name: dayCycle
new_assets.description: The planned sky cycle, three turns in 1.1 s for the months montage.
new_assets.implementation: Blend the sky presets by a phase value; sun and moon on arcs.

implementation_notes: All times are seconds on the final MP3 (157.51 s). Film length 161.0 s (end_hold 3.5 s).

Fixed marks for every doorstep dialogue: merchant x 300 facing right, friend x 600 facing left, ground y 900. Reusing the marks makes S2, S5, S7, S11 to S16 read as one place and lets the parting, the return and the confession mirror each other.

Three planted mirrors must use identical code: (1) PROMISE pose at 19.0, 131.44 and 147.12; (2) the friend's amazed poses at 37.52 and 40.24 copied by the merchant at 88.92; (3) the lie cloud (S6) and the hawk cloud (S12) share box size, tilt move and pop.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so everyone blinks; give explicit lids where a stare is held (54.72, 117.24 to 118.9).
The friend's mask: the amazed face only while the merchant is looking; when the merchant looks at the cloud or the room, let the friend's eyes check him.
Word 64.04 (التقى) is interpolated in the timeline; the boy's entrance is cued on the next word (التاجر, also listed at 64.04) and the label on 65.62.

The word at 32.60 (وعندما) and those at 41.48, 67.78, 77.00, 81.28, 98.98, 106.12 and 122.76 are listed as long (1 to 2 s) because they include a breath; the actions on them are slow arrivals, so the exact onset is not critical. Measure onsets if a hit must land exactly.
Panel-only shake for 101.6 (template pattern). Keep clouds and lettering above y 540 so they never cover a face (heads near y 690).
Use the style primitives for arrows, labels, counters, stamps and the LATER card, and call finish last.
warnings: Additions beyond the script (owner to confirm): the rat that gives the friend his idea at 42.3; the closing gag after the last word (a rat hurts its tooth on an iron nail) and the small hawk in the last sky.

The merchant taking the boy is staged as plainly kind and consensual (ball returned, hand in hand, food, a shared wink) and the cloud boy enjoys the flight (WHEEE!), so the film stays comic and never threatening.
The safe place is staged as the merchant's own house; the script does not say where it is.
Months pass by a sky and counter montage (23.02); the single LATER card is kept for A FEW DAYS LATER at 61.62.

marketStreet, merchantHouse, the person costume presets, villager, purse, ball, kneel, flush, thoughtCloud and dayCycle are planned by other stories and may not exist yet when this film is built; if not, they must be drawn here first.
Five rats plus four people is the fullest frame (S6); keep the rats inside the cloud so they stay small and simple.
